proofs.proof_tex:
We prove a uniform version, of which the asserted fixed-law convergence is an immediate consequence.  Write \(c_{a,P}\), \(\gamma_{a,P}\), and \(h_{a,P,n}\) when the dependence on the row law is material, and let \(L_{a,P}=\mathsf Z_{a,\theta,P}/f_{a,P}\), where the law of \(\mathsf Z_{a,\theta,P}\) is the law in \(\text{def:oracle-limit}\) formed with the parameters of \(P\).  Let \(d_{\mathrm{BL}}\) denote the bounded-Lipschitz distance on \(\mathbb R^R\).  We establish
\[
 \sup_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}:a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm H}\\
 P\text{ satisfies }\text{ass:gamma-separation}}}
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
 \mathcal L_P\!\left[\left\{\frac{n}{h_{a,P,n}}
 (\widehat q_a^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)-q_{a,P}(\tau))\right\}_{\tau\in\mathcal T}\right],
 \mathcal L_P(L_{a,P})\right)\longrightarrow0,
 \tag{H1}
\]
where the supremum is over gamma-separated rows obeying the displayed heavy-arm learner schedule.  All uniform statements below are with respect to this set.  For a fixed \(P\) outside that uniformly separated set, the same calculations hold with law-dependent constants and prove the theorem's stated lawwise conclusion.

First, the uniform Hall expansion in \(\text{ass:hall}\), the bounds on \(c_{a,P}\), \(\rho_{a,P}\), and \(\gamma_{a,P}\), and the definition of \(t_{a,n}\) give, by substitution followed by monotonicity,
\[
 \sup_P\left|c_{a,P}n t_{a,P,n}^{\gamma_{a,P}}-1\right|\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 h_{a,P,n}=(c_{a,P}n)^{1/\gamma_{a,P}}\{1+o(1)\}.
 \tag{H2}
\]
In particular, \(h_{a,P,n}/n\to0\) uniformly because \(\gamma_{a,P}\ge1+\epsilon_\gamma\) on the heavy regime.

Put \(Z_{i,P}=h_{a,P,n}\pi_{a,P}(X_i)\) and \(U_{i,P}=\Psi_{a,P}(Y_i)\).  Consistency and unconfoundedness imply that, conditionally on \(X_i\), the event \(A_i=a\) has probability \(\pi_{a,P}(X_i)\) and its mark has the potential-outcome score law.  Thus, for every compactly supported continuous \(g\), a Stieltjes change of variables, \(H2\), and \(\text{lem:score-law-factorization}\) give
\[
\begin{split}
 &nE_P\!\left[\mathbf1\{A_i=a\}g(Z_{i,P},U_{i,P})\right]\\
 &\quad\longrightarrow
 \int_0^\infty\!\int_{\mathbb R^R}g(z,u)H_{a,P}(du)
 (\gamma_{a,P}-1)z^{\gamma_{a,P}-1}\,dz,
\end{split}
\tag{H3}
\]
uniformly in \(P\).  Indeed, the Hall remainder is uniform on compact \(z\)-sets after scaling by \(h_{a,P,n}\), and the mark error is at most \(R\omega_{\mathrm{mark}}(z/h_{a,P,n})\), which tends uniformly to zero.  For a nonnegative \(g\), independence in \(\text{ass:iid}\) yields the exact Laplace identity
\[
 E_P\exp\!\left\{-\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf1\{A_i=a\}g(Z_{i,P},U_{i,P})\right\}
 =\left[1-E_P\{\mathbf1(A_i=a)(1-e^{-g(Z_{i,P},U_{i,P})})\}\right]^n.
 \tag{H4}
\]
Equations \(H3\)--\(H4\), using \(n\log(1-x_n)=-nx_n+o(1)\) when \(nx_n=O(1)\), prove uniform convergence of the marked point process on compact \(z\)-annuli.

Define the population-clipped oracle score
\[
 S_{a,P,n}(\tau)=\frac1{h_{a,P,n}}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \frac{\mathbf1\{A_i=a\}\psi_{a,\tau}(Y_i)}
 {\pi_{a,P}(X_i)\vee b_{a,P,n}}.
 \tag{H5}
\]
Applying \(H4\) to truncated versions of \(u_\tau/\max\{z,\theta_a\}\) and centering proves
\[
 S_{a,P,n}-E_PS_{a,P,n}\ Longrightarrow_{\mathrm{unif}}\ \mathsf Z_{a,\theta,P}.
 \tag{H6}
\]
The truncation is uniform: for \(z>C\), the centered second moment is bounded by
\(C_1\int_C^\infty z^{\gamma_{a,P}-3}dz\le C_2C^{-\epsilon_\gamma}\), while for \(z<c\) the probability of any point is bounded by
\(C_3\int_0^c z^{\gamma_{a,P}-1}dz\le C_4c^{1+\epsilon_\gamma}\).  These bounds also prove uniform tightness of the family of laws in \(H6\), including \(\theta_a=0\).

Because \(E_Pm_{a,\tau}(X)=E_P\psi_{a,\tau}\{Y(a)\}=0\), only clipping contributes to the mean.  Hall integration and \(\text{ass:tail-marks}\) give
\[
\begin{split}
 E_PS_{a,P,n}(\tau)
 &=\frac n{h_{a,P,n}}E_P\!\left[m_{a,\tau}(X)
 \left\{\frac{\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)\vee\theta_a/h_{a,P,n}}-1\right\}\right]\\
 &\longrightarrow m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}(\gamma_{a,P}-1)
 \int_0^{\theta_a}(z/\theta_a-1)z^{\gamma_{a,P}-2}\,dz\\
 &=-\frac{\theta_a^{\gamma_{a,P}-1}}{\gamma_{a,P}}
 m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}=\mu_{a,\theta,P}(\tau),
\end{split}
\tag{H7}
\]
uniformly, with the integral interpreted as zero at \(\theta_a=0\).  The sign and constant in \(H7\) follow from direct integration; no drift is included in the definition of the causal target.

The count sandwich induced by the punctured relative-error bound in \(\text{lem:boundary-likelihood}\), together with \(H2\), gives
\[
 \frac{\widehat h_{a,n}}{h_{a,P,n}}\to_P1,
 \qquad
 h_{a,P,n}\widehat p_{a,(\lceil\widehat h_{a,n}\rceil)}\to_P1,
 \qquad
 \widehat h_{a,n}\widehat b_{a,n}\to_P\vartheta_a=\theta_a,
 \tag{H8}
\]
uniformly.  To transfer the score, split at \(u_{a,n}=M_n/h_{a,P,n}\).  The reciprocal identity and the definition of \(D_{a,n}\) imply
\[
\begin{split}
 \max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}|S^{\mathrm{fe}}_{a,P,n}(\tau)-S_{a,P,n}(\tau)|
 &\le C E_{a,n}\frac1{h_{a,P,n}}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \frac{\mathbf1\{A_i=a,\ \pi_a(X_i)\le M_n/h_{a,P,n}\}}
 {\pi_a(X_i)\vee b_{a,P,n}}\\
 &\quad+\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}|D_{a,n}(\tau)|+o_P(1).
\end{split}
\tag{H9}
\]
Hall integration bounds the normalized sum in \(H9\) by \(O_P(M_n^{\gamma_{a,P}-1})\), uniformly.  Consequently, the two conclusions of \(\text{lem:boundary-likelihood}\), and specifically the corrected condition
\(E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_{a,P}-1}=o_P(1)\), make \(H9\) \(o_P(1)\).  The relative-error square-integral conclusion of that lemma gives the identical transfer for the local curvature term.

For completeness, Knight's identity follows by checking separately the signs of \(e\), \(e-v\), and zero:
\[
 \rho_\tau(e-v)-\rho_\tau(e)
 =-v\{\tau-\mathbf1(e\le0)\}
 +\int_0^v\{\mathbf1(e\le s)-\mathbf1(e\le0)\}\,ds.
 \tag{H10}
\]
Use \(e=Y_i-q_a(\tau)\) and \(v=t h_{a,P,n}/n\).  Conditional expectation, \(\text{ass:conditional-density-modulus}\), and the fact that the clipped covariate set has probability \(O(h_{a,P,n}^{1-\gamma_{a,P}})\) show, uniformly for \(t\) in compact sets and \(\tau\in\mathcal T\),
\[
 E_P\{\text{Knight remainder}\}=\frac12f_{a,P}(\tau)t^2+o(1).
 \tag{H11}
\]
The centered remainder has variance at most \(C|t|^3h_{a,P,n}/n=o(1)\), uniformly by \(H2\).  Equations \(H6\)--\(H11\) therefore give the feasible local objective
\[
 \widehat Q_{a,n,\tau}(t)
 =\frac12f_{a,P}(\tau)t^2
 -t\{\mathsf Z_{a,\theta,P}(\tau)+\mu_{a,\theta,P}(\tau)\}+o_P(1)
 \tag{H12}
\]
in the uniform bounded-Lipschitz sense, jointly over the finite set \(\mathcal T\).

It remains to verify that the correction is wholly empirical.  At
\(t_{a,k}=F_{a,P}^{\pi,-1}(k_n/n)\), uniform Hall inversion gives
\[
 t_{a,k}\asymp(k_n/n)^{1/(\gamma_{a,P}-1)},
 \qquad
 nP\{A=a,\pi_a(X)\le t_{a,k}\}\asymp k_nt_{a,k}\to\infty.
 \tag{H13}
\]
The tail-count sandwich, the uniform second-order Hall remainder, and integration of the tail empirical survival function yield
\(\widehat\gamma_a-\gamma_{a,P}=o_P(1)\).  Equation \(H13\), the common endpoint-score modulus, and the inner-fold version of the convex argument following \(H12\) yield
\(\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}|\widehat m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}-m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}|=o_P(1)\).

The density estimator has denominator divided by \(n\) converging to one.  Its kernel numerator has expectation \(f_{a,P}(\tau)+o(1)\) by the common density modulus and clipping-tail probability bound.  Its variance is bounded by
\[
 \frac C{n\omega_{a,n}}E_P\!\left[
 \frac{\pi_a(X)}{\{\pi_a(X)\vee b_{a,P,n}\}^2}\right]
 \le \frac{C h_{a,P,n}^{2-\gamma_{a,P}}}{n\omega_{a,n}}
 \le \frac{C h_{a,P,n}}{n\omega_{a,n}}=o(1).
 \tag{H14}
\]
The common conditional-density modulus also supplies a uniform upper bound on the densities at the target quantiles: choose a fixed \(v_0>0\) for which the modulus is at most one and integrate the resulting lower bound on the interval of radius \(v_0\).  Together with \(\text{ass:quantile-density}\), this justifies all uniform divisions by \(f_{a,P}\).  Moreover,
\(|\widehat q_a-q_a|/\omega_{a,n}=O_P\{h_{a,P,n}/(n\omega_{a,n})\}=o_P(1)\).  Hence
\[
 \widehat f_a-f_{a,P}=o_P(1),\qquad
 \widehat\mu_{a,\theta}-\mu_{a,\theta,P}=o_P(1)
 \tag{H15}
\]
uniformly over arms and \(\tau\).

Since the objective is convex and the curvature in \(H12\) is bounded below by \(\text{ass:quantile-density}\), the smallest minimizer is uniformly tight and the usual two-sided convexity comparison at \(t_0\pm\varepsilon\) maps \(H12\) to its unique quadratic minimizer.  Thus
\[
 \frac n{h_{a,P,n}}(\widehat q_a-q_{a,P})
 \Longrightarrow_{\mathrm{unif}}
 \frac{\mathsf Z_{a,\theta,P}+\mu_{a,\theta,P}}{f_{a,P}}.
 \tag{H16}
\]
Subtracting the empirical term in \(\text{def:drift-correction}\) and using \(H8\) and \(H15\) proves \(H1\).  Replacing fitted propensities and the empirical clip by their population counterparts deletes \(H9\) and \(H8\), respectively, and proves the stated oracle recovery.  Finally, \(\text{lem:score-law-factorization}\) shows that \(H3\) and hence the entire Lévy law use only \(H_{a,P}\), not the full endpoint conditional outcome law.

We again prove the stronger uniform moving-law expansion.  Fix a finite-variance arm \(a\), write \(q_{a,P}\), \(f_{a,P}\), and \(\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}\) when needed, and let \(L_{a,P}^{\mathrm G}\) be the centered Gaussian vector with covariance
\[
 \Sigma_{a,P}=E_P\!\left[\{\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}(O;\tau)\}_{\tau\in\mathcal T}
 \{\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}(O;\tau)\}_{\tau\in\mathcal T}^{\!\top}\right].
 \tag{G1}
\]
We show both the displayed linearization and
\[
 \sup_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}:a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}\\
 P\text{ satisfies }\text{ass:gamma-separation}}}
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
 \mathcal L_P[\sqrt n(\widehat q_a-q_{a,P})],
 \mathcal L_P(L_{a,P}^{\mathrm G})\right)\longrightarrow0,
 \tag{G2}
\]
under the stated Gaussian-arm schedules.  The uniform assertion is restricted away from \(\gamma=2\) by \(\text{ass:gamma-separation}\); for each fixed \(P\), the same proof with law-dependent constants establishes the theorem as stated.

For a log-propensity direction \(g\), direct differentiation of the Bernoulli likelihood gives
\[
 s_g(O)=\frac{\{\mathbf1(A=a)-\pi_a(X)\}g(X)}{1-\pi_a(X)},
 \qquad
 \mathcal I_{a,P}(g_1,g_2)=E_P\!\left[
 \frac{\pi_a(X)}{1-\pi_a(X)}g_1(X)g_2(X)\right].
 \tag{G3}
\]
The derivative of the signed functional is
\(\dot\Lambda_{a,P}(g)=E_P\{m_{a,\tau}(X)g(X)\}\).  Its information-space Riesz representer is
\[
 r_{a,\tau,P}(X)=m_{a,\tau}(X)\frac{1-\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)},
 \tag{G4}
\]
because substitution of \(G4\) in \(G3\) gives
\(\mathcal I_{a,P}(r_{a,\tau,P},g)=\dot\Lambda_{a,P}(g)\).  Also
\[
 E_Ps_{r_{a,\tau,P}}^2
 =E_P\!\left[m_{a,\tau}(X)^2\frac{1-\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)}\right]
 \le C_{\mathrm G}
 \tag{G5}
\]
by \(\text{ass:finite-variance}\) and \(|m_{a,\tau}|\le1\).  Thus all divisions and the projection in \(G4\) are legitimate.

Let \(r_{a,\tau,P,J}\) be the information projection of \(G4\) on the likelihood sieve.  On cells at distance \(j/J\) from the endpoint, the boundary link in \(\text{ass:boundary-link}\), the normalized local support of the B-splines, and the Hölder approximation error in \(\text{ass:holder}\) give, after summing the cellwise geometric powers,
\[
 \|s_{r_{a,\tau,P,J}}-s_{r_{a,\tau,P}}\|_{L^2(P)}=o(1),
 \tag{G6}
\]
uniformly for finite \(\gamma_{a,P}>2\), equivalently \(alpha_{a,P}<1\).  The same cell calculation and the likelihood score equation give
\[
 \sqrt n\,|\text{product approximation bias}|\le C\sqrt nJ_n^{-2s},
 \quad
 \sqrt n\,|\text{reciprocal quadratic remainder}|
 =O_P(J_n^{\alpha_{a,P}}/\sqrt n),
 \tag{G7}
\]
and the empirical Hessian replacement is
\(O_P\{J_n^{\alpha_{a,P}+1}\log n/n\}^{1/2}=o_P(1)\).  Each term is \(o_P(1)\) by the displayed tuning conditions.  If \(\gamma_{a,P}=\infty\), the fixed Hölder-ball radius and \(\pi_a=\exp(g_a)\) imply \(\inf_x\pi_a(x)\ge e^{-C}>0\).  Profiling the extra \(\log d_a\) direction against the quasi-uniform spline space gives a residual with squared norm \(O(J_n^{-1})\), a profiled coefficient error \(O_P(\sqrt{J_n/n})\), and maximum sample residual \(O_P\{\log(n/J_n)\}\); the profiled spline-function sup error is
\(O_P\{\sqrt{J_n\log J_n/n}+J_n^{-s}\}\).  Hence \(J_n\log n/n\to0\) and \(J_n^{-s}\log(n/J_n)\to0\) make the fitted propensity uniformly sample-point consistent.  This is the same profiling argument established at the mixed bounded arm in \(\text{prop:finite-variance-sanity}\), with constants uniform over the fixed Hölder ball.

For every fold, \(G3\)--\(G7\), the score equation, and the nonpositive inner product of a concave maximizer's feasible displacement with its normal-cone residual yield
\[
 \sqrt n\sum_{k=1}^K\frac{|I_k|}{n}
 \int m_{a,\tau}(x)
 \frac{\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)-\pi_a(x)}{\pi_a(x)}\,dP_X(x)
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n s_{r_{a,\tau,P}}(O_i)+o_P(1).
 \tag{G8}
\]
The coefficient is one because every observation occurs in \(K-1\) training folds, each of size \(n(K-1)/K+O(1)\).  Conditional on a training fold, cross-fitting makes the centered evaluation error mean zero.  Its conditional variance is bounded by
\[
 C\int\frac{(\widehat\pi_{a,-k}-\pi_a)^2}{\pi_a}\,dP_X
 =O_P(J_n^{-2s}+J_n^{2\alpha_{a,P}}/n)=o_P(1),
 \tag{G9}
\]
where \(2\alpha_{a,P}<\alpha_{a,P}+1\) for finite \(\gamma_{a,P}>2\), and the bounded case uses \(alpha_{a,P}=0\).

Clipping is first-order negligible.  In the bounded case, sample-point consistency and the true common lower bound make it inactive with probability tending to one.  For the following finite-\(\gamma\) comparison only, define the proof intermediate \(b^\circ_{a,P,n}=\vartheta_a/h_{a,P,n}\).  For finite \(\gamma_{a,P}>2\), \(H2\) and Hall integration give
\[
 \sqrt n\left|E_Pm_{a,\tau}(X)
 \left\{\frac{\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)\vee b^\circ_{a,P,n}}-1\right\}\right|
 \le Cn^{1/2-(\gamma_{a,P}-1)/\gamma_{a,P}}=o(1)
 \tag{G10}
\]
uniformly because \(\gamma_{a,P}\ge2+\epsilon_\gamma\).  The centered clipping difference has variance tending uniformly to zero, since
\(E_P[\pi_a(X)^{-1}\mathbf1\{\pi_a(X)\le u\}]\le Cu^{\gamma_{a,P}-2}\), obtained by Stieltjes integration of \(\text{ass:hall}\).  The same count sandwich calculation used in \(H8\), now with the finite-\(\gamma\) Gaussian exponent, shows \(\widehat b_{a,n}/b^\circ_{a,P,n}\to_P1\) when \(\vartheta_a>0\); when \(\vartheta_a=0\), both thresholds are exactly zero.  This transfers \(G10\) to the empirical threshold in both cases.

Knight's identity \(H10\), now with \(v=t/\sqrt n\), \(\text{ass:conditional-density-modulus}\), and \(\text{ass:quantile-density}\) give, uniformly on compact \(t\)-sets,
\[
 \widehat Q^{\mathrm G}_{a,n,\tau}(t)
 =\frac12f_{a,P}(\tau)t^2-
 t\,\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \left[\frac{\mathbf1(A_i=a)\psi_{a,\tau}(Y_i)}{\pi_a(X_i)}
 -s_{r_{a,\tau,P}}(O_i)\right]+o_P(1).
 \tag{G11}
\]
Using \(G4\), the bracket in \(G11\) is exactly
\[
 m_{a,\tau}(X_i)+\frac{\mathbf1(A_i=a)
 \{\psi_{a,\tau}(Y_i)-m_{a,\tau}(X_i)\}}{\pi_a(X_i)}
 =f_{a,P}(\tau)\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}(O_i;\tau).
 \tag{G12}
\]
It is centered because \(E_P\psi_{a,\tau}\{Y(a)\}=0\).

We finally verify the uniform Gaussian approximation rather than assume it.  Since \(\mathcal T\) is finite, \(G12\), the density lower bound, and \(|m|,|\psi|\le1\) reduce multivariate Lindeberg to the inverse-weight term.  For finite \(\gamma_{a,P}\ge2+\epsilon_\gamma\), Stieltjes integration of the uniform Hall bound gives, for large \(x\),
\[
 E_P\!\left[\frac{\mathbf1(A=a)}{\pi_a(X)^2}
 \mathbf1\{\pi_a(X)^{-1}>x\}\right]
 =E_P\!\left[\frac1{\pi_a(X)}\mathbf1\{\pi_a(X)<x^{-1}\}\right]
 \le Cx^{-(\gamma_{a,P}-2)}\le Cx^{-\epsilon_\gamma}.
 \tag{G13}
\]
For \(\gamma_{a,P}=\infty\), the common Hölder-ball lower bound \(\pi_a\ge e^{-C}\) makes the summands uniformly bounded.  Taking \(x\) proportional to \(\sqrt n\) in \(G13\) proves uniform Lindeberg.  For every fixed coefficient vector, expand the characteristic function of the corresponding scalar linear projection at order two on the Lindeberg-truncated event and bound the remainder by its truncated second moment.  The resulting formula is the characteristic function of the centered Gaussian vector having the row covariance \(G1\); Fourier inversion after Gaussian smoothing, followed by removal of the smoothing, gives uniform bounded-Lipschitz convergence.  No covariance convergence across rows is needed.  The lower curvature bound then maps \(G11\) to its smallest convex minimizer and yields
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat q_a(\tau)-q_{a,P}(\tau)\}
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}(O_i;\tau)+o_P(1)
 \tag{G14}
\]
jointly over the finite arm--quantile vector, with a remainder uniform in \(P\).  Equations \(G13\)--\(G14\) prove \(G2\) and the asserted covariance formula.

For a row law \(P\), define the arm vectors
\[
 W_{a,P,n}=\frac n{H_{a,P,n}}(\widehat q_a^{\mathrm{bc}}-q_{a,P}),
 \qquad
 L_{a,P}=\begin{cases}
 \mathsf Z_{a,\theta,P}/f_{a,P},&a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm H},\\
 L_{a,P}^{\mathrm G},&a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm G},
 \end{cases}
 \tag{Q1}
\]
and let \(L_P=(L_{0,P},L_{1,P})\) have the joint law supplied by the joint armwise expansion.  The heavy proof above gives uniform bounded-Lipschitz convergence for every heavy coordinate, and the Gaussian proof gives it for every finite-variance coordinate.

For a finite-\(\gamma\) Gaussian arm, the same intermediate-order survival-function calculation as in \(H13\), now with \(\gamma_{a,P}>2\), gives \(\widehat\gamma_a-\gamma_{a,P}=o_P(1)\) uniformly.  For \(\gamma_{a,P}=\infty\), the fixed Hölder ball makes \(1/\pi_a\) a uniformly bounded equicontinuous family, so its upper \(k_n/n\) order-statistic log spacings are \(o_P(1)\) and the Hill reciprocal diverges.  Gamma separation therefore gives \(P_P\{\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm G}=\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}\}\to1\) uniformly.  By \(\text{def:drift-correction}\), \(\widehat q_a^{\mathrm{bc}}=\widehat q_a\) on that event, so the Gaussian expansion applies to the coordinate in \(Q1\).

These marginal conclusions hold jointly.  For two heavy arms, \(\text{ass:opposite-overlap}\) supplies disjoint endpoint neighborhoods.  For compactly supported nonnegative \(g_0,g_1\), one observation cannot enter both endpoint point processes, so the iid Laplace transform is
\[
 \left[1-\frac{\nu_{0,P,n}(1-e^{-g_0})}{n}
 -\frac{\nu_{1,P,n}(1-e^{-g_1})}{n}+o(n^{-1})\right]^n.
 \tag{Q2}
\]
The uniform Hall and score-mark limits turn \(Q2\) into the product of the two limiting Laplace functionals, proving independence of the two heavy endpoint processes.  With one heavy and one Gaussian arm, truncate the Gaussian summands on the heavy endpoint set.  Their discarded variance tends uniformly to zero by \(\text{ass:finite-variance}\) and the Hall calculation in \(G13\).  On a retained heavy endpoint event, binary treatment makes the other arm's residual term vanish, while its regression term is bounded by one.  Hence the one-observation cross term between a compactly supported endpoint transform and the Gaussian exponential is at most \(C n^{-3/2}\); after multiplication by \(n\) it vanishes.  The joint iid characteristic function therefore factorizes, proving independence of the Gaussian and Poisson limits.  With two Gaussian arms, applying the joint characteristic-function expansion following \(G13\) to every linear projection retains the cross-arm covariance \(E_P[\mathrm{IF}_{0,P}\mathrm{IF}_{1,P}^{\top}]\).  Hence
\[
 \sup_P d_{\mathrm{BL}}\{\mathcal L_P(W_{0,P,n},W_{1,P,n}),
 \mathcal L_P(L_{0,P},L_{1,P})\}\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{Q3}
\]

The estimator definition gives the exact, nonasymptotic identity
\[
 \frac n{H_{P,n}}(\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{bc}}-\Delta_P)
 =\ell_{1,P,n}W_{1,P,n}-\ell_{0,P,n}W_{0,P,n}.
 \tag{Q4}
\]
Define the moving row law
\[
 Z_{P,n}=\ell_{1,P,n}L_{1,P}-\ell_{0,P,n}L_{0,P}.
 \tag{Q5}
\]
Since \(0\le\ell_{a,P,n}\le1\), the linear map in \(Q4\) has a uniformly bounded Lipschitz norm.  Applying it to \(Q3\) proves the strengthened conclusion requested here:
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}}
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left[
 \mathcal L_P\!\left\{\frac n{H_{P,n}}
 (\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{bc}}-\Delta_P)\right\},
 \mathcal L_P(Z_{P,n})\right]\longrightarrow0,
 \tag{Q6}
\]
under \(\text{ass:gamma-separation}\) and the armwise schedules.  No convergence of \(\ell_{a,P,n}\) is required in \(Q6\).

For the fixed \(P\) assertion, \(H2\) gives
\(h_{a,P,n}=(c_{a,P}n)^{1/\gamma_{a,P}}{1+o(1)}\).  If two fixed heavy indices are unequal, the arm with smaller \(\gamma_a\) has the larger normalization and the other coefficient tends to zero.  If they are equal, both coefficients converge and retain the ratio of Hall constants.  Since \(h_{a,P,n}/\sqrt n\to\infty\) for \(\gamma_a<2\), a heavy arm dominates a Gaussian arm.  If both arms are Gaussian, both scales are \(\sqrt n\), and their shared covariance is the one retained in \(Q3\).  Therefore, along any fixed-law subsequence with \(\ell_{a,P,n}\to\ell_a\), \(Q6\) reduces to
\[
 \frac n{H_{P,n}}(\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{bc}}-\Delta_P)
 \Rightarrow \ell_1L_{1,P}-\ell_0L_{0,P},
 \tag{Q7}
\]
which is the displayed claim.  Equation \(Q2\) proves its final independence assertion.  For varying rows with an index gap of order \(1/\log n\), neither coefficient need converge to the fixed-law dominance value; that phenomenon is governed by \(Q5\)--\(Q6\), not by replacing the row law with a single fixed limit.

We prove conditional approximation to the moving row law \(Q5\), uniformly over the class satisfying the theorem's learner schedules at \(n\) and \(m\).  This implies the stated fixed-\(P\) result and uniform pointwise coverage.  Write vectors in \(\mathbb R^{2R}\), and, at an arbitrary sample size \(N\), put
\[
 W_{P,N}^{\circ}=\left\{
 \frac N{\widehat H_{a,N}}(\widehat q_{a,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}-q_{a,P})
 \right\}_{a\in\mathcal A}.
 \tag{S1}
\]
The uniform heavy and Gaussian expansions proved above, scale consistency \(H8\), and the uniform Hill classification supplied by \(H13\) and \(\text{ass:gamma-separation}\) give a permutation-symmetric oracle leading statistic \(S_{P,N}\) such that
\[
 \sup_P P_P\{\|W_{P,N}^{\circ}-S_{P,N}\|>\varepsilon\}\to0,
 \qquad
 \sup_Pd_{\mathrm{BL}}\{\mathcal L_P(S_{P,N}),\mathcal L_P(L_P)\}\to0.
 \tag{S2}
\]
For \(\gamma=\infty\), uniform Hill classification follows without a tail assumption: the common Hölder radius makes the inverse propensity an equicontinuous, uniformly bounded family on \([0,1]\), so its upper \(k_N/N\) quantile lies uniformly within \(o(1)\) of its endpoint; hence the Hill log-spacing average is \(o_P(1)\) and \(\widehat\gamma_a\to_P\infty\).  Thus no oracle regime label enters \(S1\).

Let \(g:\mathbb R^{2R}\to[-1,1]\) be one-Lipschitz and define the complete subsample average
\[
 U_{n,m,P}(g)=\binom nm^{-1}\sum_{|b|=m}g(S_{P,b})
 =E_B\{g(S_{P,B})\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n\}.
 \tag{S3}
\]
Successively subtracting conditional expectations over proper coordinate subsets gives the orthogonal decomposition
\[
 g(S_{P,m})-E_Pg(S_{P,m})
 =\sum_{j=1}^m\sum_{|C|=j}h_{P,m,j}(O_C),
 \tag{S4}
\]
where each \(h_{P,m,j}\) has conditional mean zero given any \(j-1\) of its arguments.  If \(\zeta_{P,m,j}=E_Ph_{P,m,j}(O_1,\ldots,O_j)^2\), independence in \(\text{ass:iid}\), orthogonality in \(S4\), and counting the \(m\)-subsets containing a fixed \(j\)-subset yield
\[
\begin{split}
 \operatorname{Var}_P\{U_{n,m,P}(g)\}
 &=\sum_{j=1}^m\frac{\binom mj^2}{\binom nj}\zeta_{P,m,j}\\
 &\le\frac mn\sum_{j=1}^m\binom mj\zeta_{P,m,j}
 =\frac mn\operatorname{Var}_P\{g(S_{P,m})\}
 \le4m/n.
\end{split}
\tag{S5}
\]
The inequality uses
\(\binom mj/\binom nj\le m/n\).  Because a uniform \(m\)-subset of an iid sample has unconditionally the law of \(m\) iid observations, \(S2\), \(S3\), and \(S5\) imply
\[
 U_{n,m,P}(g)-E_Pg(L_P)\to_P0
 \tag{S6}
\]
uniformly in \(P\), for every such \(g\).

The family \(\{L_P\}\) is uniformly tight.  For Gaussian coordinates this follows from the common second-moment bound \(G5\); for heavy coordinates it follows from the small- and large-\(z\) bounds following \(H6\).  On a common compact ball, the unit bounded-Lipschitz class has a finite uniform sup-norm net.  Applying \(S5\) to that finite net and using uniform tightness outside the ball upgrades \(S6\) to
\[
 \sup_P P_P\!\left\{
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\bigl(\mathcal L_B(S_{P,B}\mid O_1^n),
 \mathcal L_P(L_P)\bigr)>\varepsilon\right\}\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{S7}
\]
Furthermore, by the same unconditional-law identity and \(S2\),
\[
\begin{split}
 &E_P\mathbb P_B\{\|W_{P,B}^{\circ}-S_{P,B}\|>\varepsilon\mid O_1^n\}\\
 &\qquad=P_P\{\|W_{P,m}^{\circ}-S_{P,m}\|>\varepsilon\}\longrightarrow0
\end{split}
\tag{S8}
\]
uniformly.  For the conditional error probability \(R_{P,n}\) in \(S8\), the elementary bound \(P_P(R_{P,n}>\eta)\le E_PR_{P,n}/\eta\) combines \(S7\)--\(S8\) into conditional uniform convergence of the refitted arm vector.

By \(\text{def:vector-subsampling}\),
\[
 V_{B,a}=W_{P,B,a}^{\circ}-C_{B,a},
 \qquad
 C_{B,a}=\frac m{\widehat H_{a,m,B}}(\widehat q_{a,n}^{\mathrm{bc}}-q_{a,P}).
 \tag{S9}
\]
Uniform tightness in \(S2\), uniform scale consistency, and \(H2\) give
\[
 \|C_{B,a}\|=O_P\!\left(\frac m{H_{a,P,m}}\frac{H_{a,P,n}}n\right)
 =\begin{cases}
 O_P\{(m/n)^{1-1/\gamma_{a,P}}\},&a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm H},\\
 O_P\{(m/n)^{1/2}\},&a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{S10}
\]
Both orders are uniformly \(o_P(1)\): in the heavy case
\(1-1/\gamma_{a,P}\ge\epsilon_\gamma/(1+\epsilon_\gamma)\).  Also
\(\max_a|\widehat\ell_{a,n}-\ell_{a,P,n}|=o_P(1)\) uniformly.  The recombination map is Lipschitz with norm at most two, so \(S7\)--\(S10\) prove exactly
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}}P_P\!\left\{
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
 \mathcal L_B(T_{B,n}\mid O_1^n),
 \mathcal L_P(Z_{P,n})\right)>\varepsilon\right\}\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{S11}
\]
This is row-wise uniform validity and does not require convergence of the recombination weights.

Fix \(\tau\in\mathcal T\).  The full-sample result \(Q6\), scale consistency, and \(S11\) compare both the normalized estimation error and the conditional statistic to the same scalar row law \(Z_{P,n}(\tau)\).  A Lipschitz approximation to a half-line shows that bounded-Lipschitz error \(delta\) changes a distribution function by at most \(delta/\eta\) plus the probability of an interval of length \(2\eta\).  The uniform quantile modulus in \(\text{ass:anti-concentration}\), first with \(eta\downarrow0\) and then with \(delta\downarrow0\), therefore gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}}
 \left|P_P\!\left\{
 c_{n,\alpha/2}(\tau)\le
 \frac n{\widehat H_n}(\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)-\Delta_P(\tau))
 \le c_{n,1-\alpha/2}(\tau)\right\}-(1-\alpha)\right|\to0.
 \tag{S12}
\]
The event in \(S12\) is exactly coverage by the displayed interval.  Since \(\mathcal T\) is finite, taking the maximum over \(\tau\) proves simultaneous convergence of the coordinatewise coverage errors.  This is not a simultaneous confidence-band assertion.

For fixed \(P\), every subsequence has a further subsequence on which the two bounded weights converge.  Equation \(S11\) then yields the fixed-law conditional limit in the theorem, and \(S12\) yields its coverage claim.  There is no contradiction with the claimed failure of uniform approximation to a single fixed limiting mixture.  To see the distinction explicitly, take the two-heavy family in \(\text{prop:smooth-inclusion}\), an interior \(\gamma\in(1,2)\), equal Hall constants, and an outcome specification whose endpoint score laws and target densities converge to fixed nondegenerate limits, and put
\[
 \gamma_{0,n}=\gamma+\frac c{2\log n},
 \qquad
 \gamma_{1,n}=\gamma-\frac c{2\log n},
 \qquad c>0.
 \tag{S13}
\]
These rows remain in the gamma-separated class with common constants.  Hall inversion gives
\[
 \log\{h_{0,P_n,n}/h_{1,P_n,n}\}
 =\{\gamma_{0,n}^{-1}-\gamma_{1,n}^{-1}\}\log n+o(1)
 \longrightarrow-c/\gamma^2.
 \tag{S14}
\]
Thus the row law in \(Q5\) retains
\(L_{1,P_n}-e^{-c/\gamma^2}L_{0,P_n}\), whereas holding any row fixed and sending a new sample size to infinity eliminates the larger-index arm.  Independence and nondegeneracy distinguish the two laws: equality of their characteristic functions near zero would force the characteristic function of a nonzero multiple of \(L_{0,P_n}\) to equal one near zero, hence that component to be degenerate.

If raw scalar subsampling uses \(m=n^\beta\), \(0<\beta<1\), then the same calculation gives
\[
 \log\{h_{0,P_n,m}/h_{1,P_n,m}\}\longrightarrow-\beta c/\gamma^2,
 \tag{S15}
\]
so it approaches the wrong mixture
\(L_1-e^{-\beta c/\gamma^2}L_0\).  In contrast, \(S11\) standardizes the refitted arms at their separate \(m\)-scales and recombines them with the full-sample weights \(\widehat\ell_{a,n}\), reproducing \(S14\).  Hence \(S13\)--\(S15\) refute only fixed-limit uniformity and simultaneously certify why the arm-vector construction repairs the moving row law.

prose_updates.tldr: A boundary-adapted growing Bernoulli likelihood preserves the compensated infinitely divisible clipped-IPW quantile law uniformly over gamma-separated rows, while the finite-variance branch admits a uniform learned-propensity Gaussian approximation. The constrained signed Riesz expansion yields the rate \(J_n^{-s}+n^{-1/2}J_n^{(\alpha_a-1)/2}+J_n^{\alpha_a}/n\) and the corrected transfer condition \(E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}=o_P(1)\). The arm laws combine into the moving row distribution \(Z_{P,n}=\ell_{1,P,n}L_{1,P}-\ell_{0,P,n}L_{0,P}\), and fully refitted arm-vector subsampling estimates this law uniformly without requiring the recombination weights to converge. The separate critical fold-labelled Poisson question remains open.

project_justification.gap: The closest weak-overlap QTE theorem uses the observed true propensity. Regular estimated-propensity quantile and series-logit results do not provide the singular Hall-boundary signed-functional expansion, a row-wise uniform learned-propensity limit away from \(\gamma=2\), or inference that remains valid under local \(1/\log n\) changes in the two arm scales.
project_justification.niche: A feasible full-population QTE procedure must preserve signed cancellation at a Hall boundary, use a positive-weight convex argmin and empirical clipping correction, retain the learned-score covariance in regular arms, and approximate the moving two-arm row law rather than a nonexistent common fixed limit.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the constrained-sieve log and signed-functional rates, proves the amplified oracle-transfer condition and its escape-perturbation necessity, establishes heavy and Gaussian arm expansions uniformly on gamma-separated rows, recombines them into \(Z_{P,n}\) without a subsequential-weight requirement, and proves uniform conditional validity of fully refitted arm-vector subsampling.

sampling_model.design: Independent superpopulation sampling under conditional unconfoundedness; identification of \(\Delta(\tau)\) is taken as given, and the contribution is row-wise limit and inference theory.
sampling_model.units: \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with a finite reported quantile set \(\mathcal T\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with arms classified as Hall-heavy or finite-inverse-moment; inference is uniform only on regimes separated from the boundary \(\gamma=2\).
sampling_model.overlap: Positivity holds almost surely. Heavy arms have a common uniform second-order Hall lower-tail expansion. Finite-inverse-moment arms with finite \(\gamma_a\) inherit a uniform Lindeberg bound from the Hall tail and gamma separation, while \(\gamma_a=\infty\) arms have a common propensity lower bound from the fixed Hölder ball.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each fold uses the constrained boundary-adapted Bernoulli series likelihood. The schedules retain \(J_N\log N/N\to0\) and \(J_N^{-s}\log(N/J_N)\to0\) at \(N=n\) and every refit size \(N=m\). Generalized-inverse scales, order-statistic clips, Hill classification, preliminary quantiles, endpoint scores, drift corrections, and densities are recomputed within each relevant sample.

prose_updates.related_work: Avella-Medina, Davis, and Samorodnitsky (2025, arXiv:2506.18215v1) provide the observed-true-propensity fixed-quantile benchmark but no feasible propensity-estimation theorem. The present class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\) is not literally their published class: it is narrower through its smooth one-dimensional boundary chart and uniform second-order Hall structure, but weaker, and therefore incomparable overall, in requiring only convergence of the finite nested quantile-score vector rather than a full conditional endpoint outcome law. The finite-\(\mathcal T\) oracle law is rederived using score-law factorization, not inherited through class inclusion. Hirano, Imbens, and Ridder (2003) motivate regular growing-likelihood projection; the proof here adds singular boundary information geometry and a uniform signed Riesz expansion. Firpo (2007) supplies regular QTE context, while the Gaussian branch here permits finite inverse moments and retains shared first-stage covariance. Heiler and Kazak (2021) motivate irregular subsampling, whereas the proved procedure refits both arm estimators and uses full-sample arm weights to recover the moving row law.
prose_updates.interpretation: The relevant inferential object for a varying law \(P\) is \(Z_{P,n}\), not a single universal weak limit. For fixed unequal heavy-tail indices, the smaller index dominates asymptotically; for gaps of order \(1/\log n\), both arms remain visible with row-dependent weights. Arm-vector refitting estimates the two marginal fluctuations at their own subsample scales and then restores the full-sample weights, which is exactly the operation needed to reproduce the row law.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The uniform theory excludes a neighborhood of \(\gamma_a=2\), uses a fixed finite quantile set, and is proved on the boundary-smooth class rather than the unrestricted Hall class. The latter is narrower than the oracle anchor in chart smoothness and uniform second-order tails but incomparable in endpoint outcomes because only the finite score-vector law is controlled. The approximation-tail condition is imposed at both full and refitted sample sizes. Coverage is pointwise in each reported quantile, with uniform convergence of finitely many coordinatewise errors, not simultaneous-band coverage. The critical fold-labelled point-process law is not asserted here.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The contribution is feasible uniform row-wise transfer and inference away from \(\gamma=2\): the constrained likelihood has the displayed signed-functional rate and corrected amplified condition; the positive-weight estimator has a compensated heavy-arm law; the finite-variance estimator has the learned-propensity influence function and a Hall-derived uniform Lindeberg bound; and the normalized QTE is uniformly bounded-Lipschitz close to \(\mathcal L_P(Z_{P,n})\). Fully refitted arm-vector subsampling consistently estimates the same moving law and gives uniform pointwise coverage under the declared anti-concentration condition. The \(1/\log n\) example refutes only approximation by fixed limiting mixtures and explains why raw scalar subsampling fails. No claim is made at \(\gamma=2\), for an infinite quantile process, or for the separate critical fold-law OEQ.

statement_notes.justification: It converts the oracle heavy-tail benchmark into a feasible growing-sieve theorem and proves uniform bounded-Lipschitz approximation to each gamma-separated row's own compensated Lévy law.
statement_notes.gap: The observed-true-propensity benchmark does not establish learned-propensity transfer or the corrected amplified condition \(E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}=o_P(1)\).
statement_notes.consumer: It supplies the uniformly controlled irregular arm coordinate used by the moving QTE row law and refitted inference.

statement_notes.justification: The likelihood Riesz projection produces the learned-propensity score contribution, while Hall tails and the bounded-propensity Hölder branch verify uniform Lindeberg rather than assuming it.
statement_notes.gap: Regular QTE theory does not provide this finite-inverse-moment profiled-sieve expansion with the data-driven clipping rule and row-specific uniform Gaussian approximation.
statement_notes.consumer: It supplies the regular coordinate and shared cross-arm covariance in mixed and two-Gaussian moving row laws.

statement_notes.justification: The exact arm-scale identity and uniform joint arm expansion prove bounded-Lipschitz approximation to \(\mathcal L_P(Z_{P,n})\) without requiring the arm weights to converge.
statement_notes.gap: The oracle benchmark does not combine two learned convex arm estimators under unequal, locally varying normalizations.
statement_notes.consumer: It defines the moving row distribution that valid refitted inference must reproduce.

statement_notes.justification: A complete-subsample variance calculation, uniform refitted arm expansions, negligible full-sample centering, and full-sample recombination prove conditional approximation to the moving row law.
statement_notes.gap: Raw scalar irregular subsampling changes the two-arm mixture under local \(1/\log n\) tail-index gaps, even though no failure occurs for the arm-vector method targeting the moving row law.
statement_notes.consumer: It yields implementable pointwise confidence intervals with coverage uniform over the declared gamma-separated class.
